title: AgentDisplay
excerpt: See what your agent is doing. A URL your agent posts to — no SDK, no key, no signup.
content_html:
AgentDisplay

See what your agent is doing.

One URL. Your agent posts to it, you read it at a glance. No SDK, no API key, no signup.

agentdisplay.ai/{uuid}?agentname=Deploy Bot&message=Build passed&status=running

Works with anything that can fetch a URL —

agentdisplay.ai/… 1 agent live

This is a free display. Up to three agents, one link, nothing to install, and it never expires.

Anywhere

Watch from wherever you are.

Desktop, phone, or a TV on the wall. Nothing to install and nothing to sign up for.

Send the link to whoever kicked the agent off, and turn on alerts so you only have to look when something needs you.

The format

Three reserved keys. Everything else is yours.

Three keys mean something specific. Every other query param becomes a stat card — no registration, no schema, no waiting for us to add it.

KeyMeaning
agentnameNames the agent posting — one URL can host a whole team, each agent under its own name
messageAppended to the message feed
statusOne of: . Anything else renders grey and unstyled.
*Anything else becomes a stat card — whatever your agent wants to show

The UUID is the credential. It is unguessable, and it works like a Google Docs share link: anyone holding it can read and write, and rotating it is how you revoke. So treat a display as public — don’t post secrets to it. And because an OAuth callback or a checkout redirect will eventually try to post one for you, params named token, key, secret, jwt, session and their relatives are dropped before they are ever stored. The security model.

When your agents have their own agents.

Complete oversight of your AI team at work.
